source_snapshot.items: UFM Telemetry TMS setup and trial run - Set up Telemetry view
source_snapshot.procedure: Open Telemetry, add a panel, edit/save a named view, optionally set a panel threshold, add/delete a panel parameter, save and change the record time.
source_snapshot.criteria: Panels and parameters can be added/deleted, and a configured threshold is displayed.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL/CONFLICTING; preserves generic UFM UI access but attaches subnet-merger/topology-deploy evidence and risk from another case.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; correctly scopes persistent telemetry-view configuration and requests explicit settings, persistence and rollback.

old_problem: The active record kept the case pending for a performance threshold oracle even though the source only validates dashboard configuration and threshold rendering; it does not use the chosen threshold as a hardware PASS criterion. NVIDIA defines view/panel/counter/time functionality, so a disposable, parameterized UI transaction is complete at review time.
disposition_reason: NVIDIA documents Telemetry views, time-series/TopX panels, monitored objects, raw/calculated counters and selectable time windows. A project owner may bind any supported harmless counter, unit, display-only threshold and record-time value in a disposable view. ED-03 permits those UI parameters, ED-08 requires real screenshots, and ED-15 prevents interpreting the display threshold as a platform acceptance limit. The rewrite removes DeepSeek's unrelated fabric-deployment risk and preserves every CRUD/persistence action.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row420 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3012 and adjacent row419 merger plus row421 live-traffic cases.
Applied NVIDIA UFM Telemetry documentation for multiple editable views, panel types, monitored objects/counters and time-range rendering.
Distinguished a display-configuration threshold from a hardware PASS threshold; no unapproved engineering limit is inferred.
Scoped all edits to a named disposable or backed-up view and retained save/reopen/delete/re-add/restore visual evidence.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row421 and verified its manifest identity; no UFM UI or fabric action ran.

test_case.test_name: Reversible UFM Telemetry view panel, parameter, threshold and record-time persistence
test_case.purpose: Prove an authorized user can create and persist a named UFM Telemetry test view, add/delete panels and parameters, display a configured threshold and change the record-time window without touching fabric topology or production dashboards.
required_package: Approved UFM endpoint/version/telemetry provider and least-privilege UI account
Named disposable test view or export/screenshot of the exact existing view for restoration
One supported object/port, panel type, counter/metric, unit, display-only threshold and record-time selection valid for that UFM release
UFM configuration/view backup or documented delete/restore method and real browser screenshot capture
test_case.test_command: Record UFM/version/provider and export or fully capture the target view prestate. In Telemetry create/open `<approved_test_view>`; add one supported panel for `<approved_object,counter,unit>`, save and reopen it. Set `<approved_display_threshold>` and `<approved_record_time>`, save/reopen and capture their rendered labels. Add then delete one supported parameter and verify each saved state after refresh; delete/re-add the disposable panel as required by the source. Finally restore the exact approved prestate or delete the disposable view, proving no NDT, topology, route, port or event-policy setting changed.
test_case.expected_result: Each bounded add/delete operation succeeds only in the target view; after save and browser refresh the exact view name, panel, metric/unit, threshold and time selection persist and render visibly. Parameter and panel deletion/re-addition behave as requested, and final restoration leaves prior views and fabric state unchanged.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires before/edit/save/reopen/restore evidence, real timestamped screenshots, exact supported metric/unit/threshold/time values and unchanged unrelated views/fabric state. A text claim, unsaved transient control, threshold without its metric/unit, or topology action cannot pass. The selected threshold is a UI-display test value, not a hardware performance verdict.
safety_gate: Use a disposable or fully backed-up view and least privilege; do not overwrite an operator dashboard
Confirm metric/unit/provider support and keep the threshold display-only unless a separate approved event policy exists
Do not enter NDT/Subnet Merger, fabric configuration or production event-policy controls
Stop on unexpected shared-view mutation, inability to restore or fabric/service impact; preserve logs and never auto-retry
expected_evidence: UFM endpoint/version/provider/account role and exact target-view identity
Prestate export or complete screenshots and chosen panel/object/counter/unit/threshold/time matrix
Timestamped real screenshots after add, save/reopen, threshold/time change, parameter delete/re-add and panel delete/re-add
Optional view/API export proving persisted values
Restored/deleted test view, unchanged fabric/config evidence and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If a save/render action fails, capture the UI/API error and current view export, stop further edits, restore the saved prestate or remove only the disposable view, and verify other views plus UFM/fabric health. Do not retry automatically or mutate topology/event policies.

source_conflict.reason: The review explicitly removes DeepSeek's unrelated subnet-merger deployment risk and evidence while preserving the source Telemetry UI intent.

blocked.reason: NVIDIA defines supported telemetry UI objects; concrete harmless values and view identity are runtime bindings.

external_authorities.title: NVIDIA UFM — Establishing Telemetry Sessions
external_authorities.applied_rule: Defines editable Telemetry views, panels, monitored objects, raw/calculated attributes and real-time/historical rendering.
